question: A 21-year-old man went to the emergency room after presenting several episodes of generalized tonic-clonic seizures in the last week. In the cranial CT scan, a unilocular cystic lesion was observed with a small nodule attached to the wall corresponding to the encysting larva of a parasite. Which of the following pathogens can be responsible ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Cystic lesion in cranial CT" -> "Possible parasitic infection" -> "Common parasites causing cystic lesions" -> "Taenia solium associated with neurocysticercosis" -> "Seizures due to cysticercosis" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Unilocular cystic lesion" -> "Indicates potential parasitic origin" -> "Taenia solium known to cause cystic lesions in the brain" -> "Seizures as a common symptom of neurocysticercosis" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Generalized tonic-clonic seizures" -> "Suggests central nervous system involvement" -> "Cystic lesions can indicate neurocysticercosis" -> "Taenia solium is the causative agent" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Cranial CT shows cystic lesion" -> "Cystic lesions can be caused by various pathogens" -> "Taenia solium is a known cause of cystic lesions" -> "Seizures are a common manifestation" -> 80%
analysis: The clinical presentation of generalized tonic-clonic seizures and the finding of a unilocular cystic lesion with a nodule in the cranial CT scan suggest a parasitic infection. The presence of a cystic lesion with a nodule is characteristic of neurocysticercosis, which is caused by the larval stage of Taenia solium, a pork tapeworm. Other options do not fit this presentation.
